title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented study settings across Kansas State University, from quiet historic reading rooms to reservable technology-equipped collaboration spaces.

cards.title: Settle Beneath the Great Room Murals
cards.subtitle: Quiet individual study on Hale Library’s third floor
cards.notes: Bring solo, concentration-heavy work and keep conversation elsewhere; this restored historic room is a designated quiet zone.
cards.short_summary: A Tudor-Gothic reading room pairs historic architecture and murals with enforced quiet-study expectations.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries identifies the third-floor Great Room as a designated quiet individual-study area with abundant study space.
cards.access_notes: Visit during Hale Library building hours. This is a quiet area intended for individual study; avoid conversation and silence devices.

cards.title: Read by the Farrell Library Windows
cards.subtitle: Natural-light study space on Hale Library’s first floor
cards.notes: Choose this room for reading or source work, with juvenile literature and curriculum materials close at hand.
cards.short_summary: A restored historic reading room combines daylight, architectural detail and nearby curriculum collections.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries says the first-floor Virginia Carlson Family Reading Room provides study space and houses juvenile literature and curriculum materials.
cards.access_notes: Located in Historic Farrell Library on Hale Library’s northwest side; use during Hale Library building hours.

cards.title: Spread Out Beside the Periodicals
cards.subtitle: Large second-floor reading room in Historic Farrell Library
cards.notes: Use the larger study area for research sessions that benefit from nearby current periodicals and Dow Center resources.
cards.short_summary: This historic second-floor room supports longer research sessions near periodicals and multicultural-study materials.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries describes Room 240 as a large study space containing the Dow Center for Multicultural and Community Studies and current periodicals.
cards.access_notes: Located on Hale Library’s second floor in Historic Farrell Library; use during building hours.

cards.entity_name: Dave and Ellie Everitt Learning Commons
cards.title: Build the Group Project on a Whiteboard Wall
cards.subtitle: Technology-rich collaboration space on Hale Library’s first floor
cards.notes: Reserve a collaboration room for team work, or use the commons’ monitors and whiteboard areas when a room is unnecessary.
cards.short_summary: Hale’s first-floor commons is configured for collaborative work with reservable rooms, displays and writable surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries says the Everitt Learning Commons has robust collaborative space, including reservable rooms, large monitors with HDMI cords and extensive whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: K-State affiliates may reserve collaboration rooms up to one month ahead for no more than four hours per day; rooms are intended for groups of two or more.

cards.entity_name: Hale Library Fourth-Floor Quiet Study Area
cards.title: Take Focus Work to the Quiet Floor
cards.subtitle: Individual study among Hale Library’s fourth-floor collections
cards.notes: Head here with headphones lowered and notifications silenced when the assignment calls for sustained, conversation-free focus.
cards.short_summary: An entire library floor is designated for quiet individual work, with both study nooks and open seating.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries designates Hale Library’s entire fourth floor as quiet study space intended for individual work.
cards.access_notes: Use during Hale Library building hours. Phones should vibrate, headphones should remain quiet and conversation belongs elsewhere.

cards.title: Claim a Graduate-Only Work Base
cards.subtitle: Individual seats, group tables and private rooms in Hale 309
cards.notes: Graduate students can use open seating on arrival or reserve a private room with an eID for focused or collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated graduate-student hub offers several work modes plus lockers and six reservable private rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries says the Grad Hub in Hale 309 is restricted to graduate students and provides individual seating, group tables and six private reservable rooms.
cards.access_notes: Graduate students only. Open seating is first-come, first-served; private rooms require a graduate student’s K-State eID to reserve.

cards.entity_name: Paul Weigel Library of Architecture, Planning and Design
cards.title: Sketch and Read in Weigel Library
cards.subtitle: Quiet, naturally lit work space in Regnier Hall 0081
cards.notes: Bring reading, drawing or laptop work when soft seating, desk space and nearby architecture and design collections fit the task.
cards.short_summary: A compact design library combines quiet seating, daylight, work surfaces, computers and specialized collections.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries says Weigel Library is open to everyone and offers quiet study space, natural light, soft seating, work spaces and computers.
cards.access_notes: Open to everyone during posted library hours. When Regnier Hall is closed, enter from the William T. Kemper Foundation Amphitheatre.

cards.title: Meet Facing the Kemper Amphitheatre
cards.subtitle: Reading and meeting area adjoining Weigel Library
cards.notes: Use the spacious commons for reading or a small meeting, especially when Weigel Library’s service desk has closed for the day.
cards.short_summary: An amphitheatre-facing commons extends the usable study setting beyond Weigel Library’s operating hours.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State Libraries describes the adjoining Pierce Information Commons as a spacious reading and meeting area that remains open after Weigel Library hours.
cards.access_notes: The commons remains open after Weigel Library closes, subject to Regnier Hall access and building schedules.

cards.title: Reserve a Two-Computer Engineering Room
cards.subtitle: Six first-floor project rooms in Fiedler Hall
cards.notes: Book one for a technical work session; every room has two computers, a table and whiteboard, while three add presentation displays.
cards.short_summary: Six reservable engineering study rooms support shared computer work, whiteboarding and presentation practice.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carl R. Ice College of Engineering documents six reservable first-floor Fiedler Hall study rooms with two computers, tables and a whiteboard in each.
cards.access_notes: Available by reservation through the Student Help Desk in Fiedler Learning Commons; building access follows Engineering complex hours.

cards.entity_name: College of Business Building Study Rooms
cards.title: Find a First-Come Business Study Room
cards.subtitle: Private and technology-equipped rooms across floors two through four
cards.notes: Arrive during building hours and choose a room sized for the task; technology rooms add displays and laptop connections.
cards.short_summary: The Business Building offers open study areas plus rooms ranging from simple table setups to display-equipped spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: K-State’s College of Business says its study rooms on floors two through four are available to all K-State students on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.access_notes: No reservations; rooms are first-come, first-served for K-State students during posted College of Business Building hours.
